Belly Foods

Project Overview

Belly app is a revolutionary food service platform that has something for everyone. Whether you're a food vendor looking to expand your reach or a customer looking for a quick and easy way to order food, Belly has you covered.

My Roles
  • Defined the goals of UX research.
  • Conducted user interviews and surveys to understand customer needs and pain points.
  • Designed the overall layout and navigation of the app to make it easy for users to find and order their favorite dishes.
  • Collaborated with the marketing team to create promotional materials and campaigns that drive app usage and retention.

For vendors, Belly offers a simple and intuitive interface that allows you to add and manage your menus, update your restaurant's information, and track orders in real-time. With Belly, you can offer your customers a variety of options including take-out, dine-in, and delivery. You can even use Belly's promotional tools to attract new customers and increase sales.

For customers, Belly makes it easy to discover new restaurants and explore menus. With a few taps of your phone, you can find the perfect restaurant and place an order for take-out, dine-in, or delivery. You can also use Belly to earn credits and rewards, track your orders, and read and write reviews.

Competitive Analysis findings

Before starting with the app, I checked out the existing apps. Almost all food ordering apps offer similar features and services with some difference in their selection of restaurants, cuisines, search filters, and promotional offers. Some of the key features are:

  • Easy login (Google and Facebook)
  • Restaurant and menu listings: The app should provide users with a comprehensive list of restaurants. The user should be able to browse through the menu along with description, images and price.
  • Real time Order Tracking: The app should provide users with the status of their orders in real time.
  • Order History: The app should store user’s order history, allowing them to easily reorder their favorite meals.

Restaurant listings

Search and filter restaurants by location, price, and rating. View restaurant hours of operation, address and contact info.

Menu listings

Browse menu items by category such as appetizers, entrees, desserts. Add items to cart for checkout.

Order management

Real time order tracking from placement to delivery. Push notifications for status updates. Reorder from past orders with ease. Leave feedback and ratings for completed orders.

Takeaways

User testing is key.
When conducting user testing, it's important to use realistic scenarios that mimic real-world usage. User testing should be started as early in the development process as possible, and should be conducted frequently.
After conducting user testing, it's important to use the feedback received to make improvements to the app. This can involve tweaking the design, adding new features, or addressing usability issues. By iterating based on user feedback, app created can be more user-friendly and will meet the needs of the target audience.

Next Steps

The next step would be to conduct another round of usability studies with a wider range of participants, to determine whether the current solution effectively addresses the users’ pain points.
